tests_summary: 1951/1951 npm test green (0 failed, 0 skipped), measured on this tree by scripts/run-tests.mjs, which runs `node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` and writes the counts it read from the runner's own summary block to jev-artifacts/test-measurement.json. The number is composed into this record from that file on every run, so it cannot outlive the suite it describes. The gates it covers: five pack facets' proof lines, the ledger's declared baseline resolving, one job writing only its own result, a non-passing recorded step cutting the run short, the live model pinned rather than aliased, one run described one way, and a run that never called the provider read as a configuration gap rather than a provider error. deploy:check stages the build clean.
ci_summary: This head: 1951/1951 tests, 232/232 browser smoke gates, prettier, seo, plan:check, check-chars, deploy:check and gate:byte-budgets green, CodeQL green, Jev report attached. Every count here is composed from the run that produced this record, and every stated fact about shipped bytes is checked against the tree by scripts/check-evidence-freshness.mjs, which fails the build if the record states a count or a stamp the tree contradicts. The jev-complete job runs on pull_request only, needs every gate job this workflow runs plus always() so a red gate still produces a record, and writes its evidence and report to runner temp storage so the checkout stays clean.

the `performance` facet line was REMOVED from the former JSON facet_evidence field, and is deliberately not replaced by a typed line. It was the only axis whose proof line was a hand-typed PROXY - 'eager first-load JS is 786,390 bytes against the 790,000 budget, 3,610 headroom. Perf suite 4/4' - describing bytes rather than a measured first paint, and it went unread while a real Lighthouse measurement existed as a CI artifact. The Lighthouse gate (Q-02, P0.4) now composes this line from the run that measured it: the report declares facet_axes and carries a composed facet_line, and build-jev-evidence.mjs derives the axis from the gate reports in the artifacts directory, so the numbers on the judge's record and the numbers in the report cannot drift apart. A missing report leaves the axis absent, which the judge reads as unverified and never as proven. tests/jev-derived-facets.test.mjs fails the build if a typed `performance` line returns to this file

the `experience` facet line was REMOVED from the former JSON facet_evidence field, on the same terms as `performance`. It was a sentence about TEST COVERAGE (30 of 153 smoke gates are battery-only), which is a true fact about this repo and a statement about nothing a visitor ever touches. The demand for the axis named four observable things - walk the first-run flow, make actions acknowledge themselves, give errors a next step, and invite rather than confuse in empty states - and not one of them is a fact about how many tests exist. scripts/check-experience.mjs (P0.4) now drives the staged build through the nine-step journey, provokes the reachable errors, reads the empty surfaces, and sweeps the DOM for dictionary keys painted into the page; its report declares facet_axes and carries a composed facet_line. On its first walk it found two surfaces rendering their own i18n key to the visitor and two error messages that named a failure with no way out of it. The walk found them because nothing else had walked the journey: all of it sat inside a panel that quick mode hides, so nothing that looked at the landing frame could see it. A missing report leaves the axis absent, which is read as unverified and never as proven. tests/jev-derived-facets.test.mjs fails the build if a typed experience line returns

the `translation` facet line was REMOVED from the former JSON facet_evidence field, and the axis now belongs to scripts/check-experience.mjs, which composes it from the run. The typed line was 1233 characters against a 280-character transport clip, so the judge was reading its first clause — a sentence about scripts/check-i18n.mjs and key parity — cut off mid-sentence, while six locales of measured copy sat unread under the `experience` heading. Two stories about one facet, and the one being read was the weaker. What the judge asked for verbatim is "no raw key name reaching a visitor", which is a question about a rendered surface and only a browser can answer it. PARITY IS NOT LOST WITH THE LINE, it moved to the `i18n` axis and to scripts/check-i18n.mjs, which still runs inside npm run seo and still gates both-direction parity and placeholder integrity; the composed line names it rather than claiming it. The line's account of the ten strings that existed only in the translated dictionaries, of tariffNote being built from an English template literal, and of de.tariffNote being missing entirely, is history and is kept in the ledger. STILL OPEN and not claimable here: back-reading all rendered strings for meaning remains incomplete, and native-speaker review remains open. P5.5/R-I18N-06 now ships on this branch; scripts/check-experience.mjs measures its staged locale/page/key draft path and verifies that it sends no request.

This semantic review is not native-speaker review; broader translated prose review remains open. See docs/jev-completion/CHART_TRANSLATION_BACKREAD_2026-10-22.md.
